column1: # Phase 3 milestone G follow-up: the scheduled block-tick loop's golden run
# parameters.
# NOT a vanilla dump: what a fire schedules is `30 + random.nextInt(10)` from the
# level's own `RandomSource`, whose state on any tick belongs to the server, so
# this is a regression pin of this runtime's own behaviour rather than a
# comparison against the game jar. `ctest -R block_tick` replays every row
# below through the real `BlockTickQueue` and the real dispatch
# (`run_block_tick_position`'s shape: a fire ticks as fire, a leaf as a leaf,
# anything else is dropped), and compares the whole trace line for line, so a
# reschedule one tick early or a dropped entry that silently ran cannot land.
# Regenerate deliberately with `plusmc-block-tick-dump <fixtures_dir>`, reading
# `--diff`'s patch first.
# `ticks` is how many world ticks the run advanced the queue through (one
# `advance()` each), `schedules`/`due`/`drops`/`writes`/`reads` are the counts
# of those trace rows, `draws`/`units` the two halves of the recorded stream
# (integer and float draws) and `endPending`/`endChunks` the queue's own state
# after the last tick — a fire that survives is still pending, and a settled
# chop is zero, `blob` (two adjacent leaves whose log is gone) included: its
# last recompute changes nothing, and a write that changes nothing is skipped
# the way `LevelChunk.setBlockState`'s unchanged-state early return skips it
# (the tool's header has the branch and its history). `rows` is the trace's
# length.
